Chemical Reactions

  • Chemical reactions are processes where substances (reactants) transform into new substances (products) through the breaking and forming of chemical bonds.
  • They can be classified as: Exothermic and Endothermic Reactions.

Exothermic Reactions and Endothermic Reactions

Exothermic ReactionsEndothermic Reactions
A reaction that releases energy from the system in the form of heatA reaction in which the system absorbs energy from its surrounding in the form of heat
Exo means "out"Endo means "in"

Types of Chemical Reaction

  1. 1. Combination Reaction (most combination reactions are exothermic)
  • It is a chemical reaction where a single product is formed from two or more reactants.
  • CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ (aq) + Heat (Quick Lime → Slaked Lime; it is an exothermic reaction)
  • Neutralisation is an exothermic reaction. E.g. mixing acid and alkali.
  • Ca(OH)₂ reacts slowly with CO₂ in the air to form thin layer of CaCO₃ (Calcium carbonate gives shiny finish to walls). Other names for CaCO₃ are: Chalk/Marble/Limestone.
  • Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O (Lime Water)
  • CO₂ turns lime water milky.
  1. 2. Other Examples of Exothermic Reactions
  • Burning of coal (Combustion and Combination Reaction).
  • Burning of natural gas [Primary component: CH₄ (methane)]: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O
  • Burning of magnesium ribbon (Combination Reaction): 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO + Heat + Light (white dazzling light; white ppt formed)
  • Mg is cleaned before burning in air, because it reacts with atmospheric O₂ to form MgO, which prevents further reaction with O₂.
  • Mg is used in fireworks because it burns very hot and bright.
  • Respiration is also an exothermic reaction: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + Energy (Glucose)
  1. 3. Combustion Reaction
  • It is a type of chemical reaction, where a substance reacts with oxygen gas releasing energy in the form light and heat.
  • C + O₂ → CO₂
  • Combustion reaction always takes place in presence of oxygen.
  1. 4. Decomposition Reaction
  • It is a type of chemical reaction, where single compound breaks down into two or more simpler products, often requiring energy in the form of heat, light, electricity.

(a) Thermal Decomposition

  1. 1. 2FeSO₄ →(Δ) Fe₂O₃ + SO₂ (g) + SO₃ (g) (Endothermic) (Ferrous Sulphate → Ferric Oxide)
  2. 2. CaCO₃ →(Δ) CaO + CO₂ (Oxygen was discovered by Joseph Priestley)
  3. 3. 2Pb(NO₃)₂ →(Δ) 2PbO + 4NO₂ (g) + O₂ (g) (Lead Nitrate → Lead Oxide; Brown Fumes of NO₂)

(b) Electrolysis

  • Electrolysis of water: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂ (At Cathode / At Anode)
  • H₂ gas collected is double the amount of O₂
  • Water used in electrolysis: Pure water, acidified water, distilled water.

(c) Photolysis

  • 2AgCl →(Sun) 2Ag + Cl₂
  • 2AgBr →(Sun) 2Ag + Br₂
  • They are kept in dark bottle. AgCl and AgBr are used in black and white photography. A photogenic film is coated with the chemicals. When light falls on the surface of the film, the exposed part of the film is darkened, from which photograph is developed.
  1. 5. Displacement Reaction
  • It is a type of chemical reaction in which a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound. E.g. Zn and Pb are more reactive element than Cu.
  • Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu
  • Pb + CuCl₂ → PbCl₂ + Cu
  • Mg (s) + ZnSO₄ (aq) → MgSO₄ (aq) + Zn (s)

Reactivity Series

  • Potassium (K)
  • Sodium (Na)
  • Calcium (Ca)
  • Magnesium (Mg)
  • Aluminium (Al)
  • Zinc (Zn)
  • Iron (Fe)
  • Lead (Pb)
  • Hydrogen (H)
  • Copper (Cu)
  • Mercury (Hg)
  • Silver (Ag)
  • Gold (Au)

(Reactivity decreases)

  • Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu
  • The colour of CuSO₄ solution changes when an iron nail is dipped in it. The iron nail becomes brownish and blue colour of CuSO₄ turns green.

5. Double Displacement Reaction

  • It is a type of chemical reaction in which two compounds exchange their ions to form two new compounds. It is also sometimes called Precipitation Reaction when one of the products is an insoluble solid (precipitate).
  • Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → BaSO₄ + NaCl (White ppt)
  • Pb(NO₃)₂ + KI → PbI₂ + KNO₃ (Yellow ppt)
  • Ba(OH)₂ + NH₄Cl → BaCl₂ + NH₄OH (Endothermic)

6. Oxidation Reaction

  • Oxidation reaction is addition of oxygen and removal of hydrogen.
  • Fe + O₂ →(Δ) Fe₂O₃ (Oxidation / Reduction)

7. Reduction Reaction

  • Reduction reaction is removal of oxygen and addition of hydrogen.
  • PbO + C → 2Pb + CO₂ (Reduction / Oxidation)
  • Oxidizing Agent (Oxidant): PbO because it gives oxygen to carbon.
  • Reducing Agent (Reductant): C because it removes oxygen from PbO.

Redox Reaction

  • A redox (oxidation-reduction) reaction is a chemical process in which electrons are transferred between chemical substances.
  • In redox reaction, one substance being oxidized (losing electrons) and another being reduction (gaining electrons).
  • The oxidised substance is called reducing agent since it facilitates by donating electrons, while the reduced substance is the oxidising agent, as it accepts electrons.
  • Cr₂O₇²⁻ + SO₃²⁻ → Cr³⁺ + SO₄²⁻ (+6 → +3 reduction; +4 → +6 oxidation)

Corrosion

  • A corrosion is a process of deterioration of metal as a result of its reaction with air or water (present in environment) surrounding it.
  • E.g. 4Fe + 3O₂ + xH₂O → 2Fe₂O₃ · xH₂O
  • When iron corrodes or rust, iron molecules react with oxygen molecules to form iron oxide. Rust is a reddish brown, flaky substance that forms on the surface of the iron. Technically, a rust is Hydrated Iron (III) Oxide whose chemical formula is Fe₂O₃ · xH₂O. Corrosion of iron is commonly known as rusting.
  • 2Cu + H₂O + CO₂ + O₂ → Cu(OH)₂ + CuCO₃
  • Copper metal when exposed to air turns green in color due to corrosion. When the copper vessel is exposed to air in the rainy season, the metal reacts with gases, moisture and atmospheric gases to form a mixture of CuCO₃ and Cu(OH)₂. This gives a green color to the surface of Copper metal.

Rancidity

  • It is a type of oxidation reaction.
  • It is the process by which fats and oils in food breakdown, resulting in unpleasant smell, taste, or texture. E.g. Nitrogen gas is used in chips packets to prevent oxidation, which may cause chips to become stale and soggy.

Note

Hydrogen has more than one oxidation number: +1 and -1.

Calculation of Oxidation Number

FormulaEquationSimplifiedx (Oxidation state)
N₂O₅2x + 5(-2) = 02x - 10 = 0x = 5
CaOx + (-2) = 0x = 2
MnO₂x + (-2) × 2 = 0x = 4
NaAlH₄1 + x + 4(-1) = 0x + 1 - 4 = 0x = 3
H₂S₂O₇(-2) + 2x - 14 = 02x = 16x = 8

x: Oxidation state
